# QR codes

## What it's for

Event tickets, check-in links, a table's ordering page, a Wi-Fi login: a QR code your users scan from a screen or
paper. The module draws one as an SVG image from any text, with the
[qrcode](https://crates.io/crates/qrcode) crate. SVG stays sharp at any size and prints well.

## The route

An API route that gives a ticket's owner their ticket's QR code. `tickets` has a `code` text field and an `owner`
relation to `users`:

```ts
// pb_pages/tickets/[id]/qr.ts: a ticket's QR code, for its owner, as SVG
export async function get(ctx: any) {
  if (!ctx.auth) throw ctx.httpError(401, "Sign in first")
  const ticket = ctx.app.findRecordById("tickets", ctx.params.id)
  if (ticket.get("owner") !== ctx.auth.id) throw ctx.httpError(403, "Not your ticket")
  const svg = await $wasm.run.async<string>("qrcode", `https://example.com/check-in/${ticket.get("code")}`)
  return ctx.res.json({ svg })
}
```

A plain `<img src>` doesn't send the user's PocketBase token, so fetch the SVG with it (the JS SDK's `pb.send`)
and show it from a blob URL (`new Blob([svg], { type: "image/svg+xml" })`). Or draw it once, when the ticket is created, and save it in a protected file field:
then an `<img>` with a [file token](https://pocketbase.io/docs/files-handling/#protected-files) shows it.

## The module

The text is stdin; the SVG is stdout ([`src/main.rs`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/wasm/example/qrcode/src/main.rs)):

```rust
let code = QrCode::with_error_correction_level(&input, EcLevel::M)
    .unwrap_or_else(|e| fail("too_long", &format!("can't encode it: {e}")));
let image = code.render::<svg::Color>().min_dimensions(200, 200).build();
std::io::stdout().write_all(image.as_bytes()).unwrap();
```

Error correction `M` survives about 15% of the code being damaged or covered. Change the colors with
`.dark_color(svg::Color("#1d4ed8"))`.

## Build

```sh
cd ext/wasm/example/qrcode
cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1   # rustup target add wasm32-wasip1 first
cp target/wasm32-wasip1/release/qrcode.wasm pb_hooks/qrcode.pb.wasm
```

## Cost

109 KB. The first call compiles it (about 30 ms); later calls load it from the cache in about 1.3 ms and draw a code in about 2 ms.

## Limits

- A QR code holds at most 2,331 bytes at level `M`; longer text fails with `too_long`.
- An empty input fails with `empty_input`.
